stem: A company adopts Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for its analytics teams. The marketing and finance business units must each control their own blueprints and membership. Individual teams within each business unit need isolated workspaces that have their own data and compute. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a separate SageMaker Unified Studio domain for each team. Add all users to every domain, and control access with IAM policies.
Create one domain for the company. Create a domain unit for each business unit and a project for each team.
Create a SageMaker Unified Studio project for each business unit. Create a nested domain inside each project for each team.
Create a SageMaker Unified Studio domain for each business unit. Use IAM groups instead of projects to separate the teams.

explanation: B is correct. A single domain represents the organization, domain units model the business units and own their own blueprints and membership, and projects give each team an isolated workspace with its own data and compute. A is wrong because a domain per team eliminates the business unit layer and forces membership and blueprints to be managed separately in every domain. C is wrong because the hierarchy is inverted; a domain contains projects, and a domain cannot be created inside a project. D is wrong because IAM groups do not create workspaces, project catalogs, or compute isolation in SageMaker Unified Studio.

stem: A company registers a data lake that contains 400 AWS Glue Data Catalog tables with AWS Lake Formation. Teams add new tables every week. The company must grant each analyst group access based on the sensitivity classification of the tables, and it does not want to issue a new grant every time a table is added. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Grant Lake Formation SELECT permissions on each table to each analyst group. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to repeat the grants for new tables.
Create an IAM policy for each analyst group that lists the Amazon S3 prefixes of the tables that match each sensitivity classification.
Create a separate Lake Formation data lake location for each sensitivity classification. Move each table's data into the matching location.
Define LF-Tags for sensitivity, assign the tags to databases and tables, and grant permissions on LF-Tag values.

explanation: D is correct. Lake Formation tag-based access control grants permissions on LF-Tag expressions, and a new table inherits the LF-Tag of its database, so existing grants cover the table as soon as it is created. A is wrong because it keeps per-table grants and adds custom code that must run after every table is created. B is wrong because Amazon S3 prefix permissions bypass the Data Catalog and must still be edited for every new table. C is wrong because it forces the data to be physically reorganized by classification and still requires new grants whenever a table changes classification.

stem: A company registered an Amazon S3 data lake location with AWS Lake Formation and revoked the IAMAllowedPrincipals grants on all tables. An analyst who has no Lake Formation grants can still query the data with Amazon Athena. The analyst's IAM role includes a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the data lake bucket. The company must make Lake Formation permissions the only control on table access. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Remove the s3:GetObject permission for the data lake bucket from the analyst's role.
Add a Lake Formation deny grant for the analyst's IAM role.
Add the analyst's IAM role to the Lake Formation data lake administrators list.
Turn off the query result reuse feature in the analyst's Athena workgroup.

explanation: A is correct. Lake Formation controls are effective only when principals have no independent Amazon S3 access to the registered location; removing s3:GetObject leaves Lake Formation credential vending as the only path to the data. B is wrong because Lake Formation permissions are grants only and there is no deny grant to create. C is wrong because data lake administrators receive broad permissions over the catalog, which would increase the analyst's access instead of restricting it. D is wrong because query result reuse affects cached query results and has no effect on the analyst's access to the underlying table or objects.

stem: A data engineer must give a team of analysts read-only access to all tables in the sales schema of an Amazon Redshift cluster. Engineers create new tables in the schema every week. The analysts must be able to query the new tables without any additional action from the data engineer. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a role for the analysts. Grant SELECT on all existing tables in the sales schema, and run a daily stored procedure that grants SELECT on new tables.
Create a role for the analysts. Grant USAGE on the sales schema and SELECT on all tables, and use ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for future tables.
Create a role for the analysts. Grant the SUPERUSER attribute to the role so that the analysts can read every table in the cluster.
Create a role for the analysts. Grant SELECT on a late-binding view for each table, and re-create the views when engineers add tables.

explanation: B is correct. USAGE on the schema plus SELECT on all tables covers the existing tables, and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES makes the tables that the engineers create later inherit the same SELECT grant automatically. A is wrong because a daily stored procedure is custom code, and new tables remain inaccessible until the next run. C is wrong because SUPERUSER confers full write and administrative control over the cluster, which breaks the read-only requirement. D is wrong because a view for every table must be re-created whenever engineers add a table, which is more ongoing work than default privileges.

stem: A data engineering team hardcodes a database user name, a database password, and an Amazon S3 output path in the job parameters of several AWS Glue jobs. The team must remove the plaintext password from the job parameters and must store the non-sensitive values at no additional charge. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Store the database password in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the Glue job role permission to retrieve the secret.
Store the database password in an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameter of type String.
Store the output path in an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameter, and read it in the job.
Store the output path in an AWS Secrets Manager secret, and read the secret each time that the job runs.
Store the database password in an encrypted Amazon S3 object, and have the job download the object at run time.

explanation: A is correct. Secrets Manager is purpose-built for credentials, and the Glue job role can retrieve the password at run time so no plaintext password remains in the job parameters. C is correct. Parameter Store standard parameters hold non-sensitive configuration such as an output path at no additional charge. B is wrong because a String parameter stores the password in plaintext, which leaves the credential exposed to anyone who can read the parameter. D is wrong because Secrets Manager charges per secret per month, which adds cost for a value that is not sensitive. E is wrong because an S3 object is not a credential store; the job still needs permissions to read it, and updating the password becomes a manual file operation.

stem: A data analyst must run Amazon Athena queries against one AWS Glue Data Catalog database and its underlying Amazon S3 prefix. The security team rejected the AmazonAthenaFullAccess managed policy because it grants access to every database in the account. The analyst must not be able to query any other data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach the AmazonAthenaFullAccess managed policy to the analyst's role, and add a permissions boundary that allows all Athena actions in the account.
Attach the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy to the analyst's role, and rely on Athena to block access to the other databases.
Create a customer managed policy that allows Athena actions on one workgroup, Glue actions on that database, and reads on the prefix.
Create an IAM user for the analyst. Attach the AWSGlueConsoleFullAccess and AmazonAthenaFullAccess managed policies to the user.

explanation: C is correct. A customer managed policy can scope Athena actions to a single workgroup, Glue actions to the ARNs of that database and its tables, and s3:GetObject to one prefix, which is the least privilege the security team requires. A is wrong because a permissions boundary that allows all Athena actions does not narrow the managed policy, so access to other databases remains. B is wrong because AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess grants reads on every bucket in the account, and Athena does not restrict databases on its own. D is wrong because both managed policies grant account-wide access, and creating an IAM user adds long-lived credentials without limiting scope.

stem: A company has many AWS Glue jobs that belong to different project teams. Each Glue job is tagged with a Project key. Engineers must be able to start only the jobs that belong to their own project. The company adds new projects frequently and does not want to update IAM policies for each new project. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM role for each project. List the ARNs of that project's Glue jobs in the role's policy for the glue:StartJobRun action.
Create an IAM group for each project. Attach an inline policy that allows glue:StartJobRun on all jobs, and add a deny statement for other projects' jobs.
Create an AWS Lambda function that checks each engineer's project before the function calls the glue:StartJobRun API operation on the engineer's behalf.
Tag each engineer's IAM role with a Project key. Allow glue:StartJobRun when aws:ResourceTag/Project matches aws:PrincipalTag/Project.

explanation: D is correct. Attribute-based access control compares the principal tag on the engineer's role with the resource tag on the Glue job, so a single policy authorizes every new project as soon as the job and the role carry matching tags. A is wrong because the ARN list must be edited whenever a job or a project is added. B is wrong because the deny statements must be updated for each new project, and a blanket allow on all jobs is not least privilege. C is wrong because it builds and maintains a custom authorization service in Lambda instead of using an IAM condition that AWS evaluates.

stem: Two teams share one Amazon EMR on EC2 cluster and submit Spark jobs as EMR steps. The data is in an Amazon S3 data lake that is registered with AWS Lake Formation. Each team must access only the tables that Lake Formation grants to that team, but all jobs currently run with the cluster's EC2 instance profile. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable runtime roles for the cluster. Submit each job with the team's IAM role that has the Lake Formation grants.
Create one EMR cluster for each team. Attach an EC2 instance profile that has full access to the data lake bucket.
Add both teams' IAM roles to the trust policy of the cluster's EC2 instance profile. Grant Lake Formation permissions to the instance profile.
Add an Amazon S3 bucket policy that allows each team's IAM role to read only the prefixes that hold that team's tables.

explanation: A is correct. EMR runtime roles let each step run with the submitting team's IAM role instead of the shared instance profile, and EMR integrates that role with Lake Formation so table grants are enforced per team on one cluster. B is wrong because a cluster per team costs more and the instance profile still grants full data lake access, which ignores Lake Formation grants. C is wrong because changing a trust policy does not change the identity that the steps use, so both teams still share one identity. D is wrong because prefix-level bucket policies bypass the Data Catalog and cannot express table-level or column-level grants.

stem: A company stores data in an Amazon S3 bucket in its data account. The bucket uses server-side encryption with an AWS KMS customer managed key in the same account. An AWS Glue job that runs in a separate analytics account must read the objects. The Glue job role currently receives an AccessDenied error. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable an S3 Bucket Key on the bucket so that the Glue job role can decrypt objects without any KMS permissions.
Create a KMS grant that allows the Amazon S3 service principal to decrypt objects for any principal in the analytics account.
Update the bucket policy to allow s3:GetObject for the Glue job role in the analytics account.
Copy the KMS key to the analytics account, and encrypt the objects again with the copied key.
Update the KMS key policy to allow kms:Decrypt for the Glue job role in the analytics account.

explanation: C is correct. Cross-account access to an S3 bucket requires a resource policy grant, so the bucket policy must allow s3:GetObject for the Glue job role in the analytics account. E is correct. The objects are encrypted with a customer managed key, so the key policy in the data account must allow kms:Decrypt for that same role. A is wrong because an S3 Bucket Key only reduces the number of KMS requests and grants no principal permission to decrypt. B is wrong because a grant is issued to a specific grantee principal, and permitting the S3 service principal does not authorize a role in another account. D is wrong because KMS keys cannot be copied to another account, and re-encrypting the data would duplicate it rather than share it.

stem: A company encrypts a data lake in Amazon S3 with server-side encryption that uses an AWS KMS customer managed key. Amazon Athena queries read millions of small objects each day, and the company's AWS KMS charges have increased sharply. The company must reduce the KMS request charges but must keep using its customer managed key. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Switch the bucket to server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) for all new objects.
Turn on S3 Bucket Keys for the bucket to reduce requests to AWS KMS.
Create a new KMS key in each Region, and configure S3 Cross-Region Replication to spread the requests.
Enable automatic annual rotation of the customer managed key to lower the per-request charge.

explanation: B is correct. An S3 Bucket Key is a short-lived bucket-level key that Amazon S3 derives from the KMS key, so S3 calls KMS once per bucket key instead of once per object, which sharply reduces request charges while the objects stay protected by the customer managed key. A is wrong because SSE-S3 abandons the customer managed key that the company must keep. C is wrong because replicating to another Region adds storage cost and generates KMS requests in both Regions. D is wrong because key rotation creates new key material on a schedule and has no effect on KMS request pricing.

stem: An Amazon Redshift table stores full credit card numbers. Analysts must see only the last four digits of each number, and the fraud investigation team must see the full value. The company must not create a second copy of the table and must not change the queries that the teams already run. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a view that applies a substring function to the column. Grant the analysts access to the view, and revoke their access to the table.
Encrypt the column with the AWS Encryption SDK before the data is loaded. Give the fraud team the AWS KMS key.
Create a dynamic data masking policy on the column that returns the last four digits. Attach the policy to the analyst role.
Create a row-level security policy on the table. Attach the policy to the analyst role so that masked rows are hidden.

explanation: C is correct. Amazon Redshift dynamic data masking attaches a masking policy to a column for a specific role, so the analyst role sees only the last four digits while the fraud team role, which has no masking policy attached, still sees the full value; both teams query the same table with unchanged SQL. A is wrong because the analysts would have to query a different object, which changes their existing queries. B is wrong because client-side encryption stores ciphertext, breaks the existing queries, and cannot reveal a partial value. D is wrong because row-level security filters which rows are returned and cannot mask part of a column value.

stem: A company must encrypt data at rest on the local disks of an Amazon EMR cluster and must encrypt data in transit between the cluster nodes. The cluster runs Spark jobs that read from and write to Amazon S3. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an Amazon EMR security configuration that enables at-rest encryption for local disks with an AWS KMS key.
Attach an IAM policy to the EMR service role that denies any request that does not use the aws:SecureTransport condition key.
Enable Amazon S3 default encryption on the cluster's log bucket, and turn on server access logging for the bucket.
In the security configuration, turn on in-transit encryption and provide TLS certificates in a .zip file in Amazon S3.
Launch the cluster in a private subnet, and use a security group that allows traffic only between the cluster nodes.

explanation: A is correct. An EMR security configuration turns on local disk encryption with an AWS KMS key for the storage that the cluster nodes use. D is correct. The same security configuration turns on in-transit encryption, which requires TLS certificates that EMR reads from a .zip file in Amazon S3 or from a custom certificate provider. B is wrong because aws:SecureTransport applies to API requests to services such as Amazon S3 and does nothing for local disks or internode traffic. C is wrong because encrypting the log bucket and enabling access logging protect neither the cluster's local disks nor traffic between nodes. E is wrong because network isolation limits who can reach the nodes but leaves the traffic between them unencrypted.

stem: A company must upload files from an on-premises server to Amazon S3. A compliance rule states that the data must be encrypted with the company's AWS KMS key before the data leaves the company's data center, and that AWS must never receive the plaintext data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use the AWS Encryption SDK with the KMS key to encrypt each file before the upload.
Upload the files over an AWS Direct Connect connection, and turn on server-side encryption with the KMS key.
Upload the files with the AWS CLI over HTTPS, and turn on S3 default encryption with the KMS key.
Use AWS DataSync with a TLS-enabled task, and turn on server-side encryption with the KMS key on the destination bucket.

explanation: A is correct. The AWS Encryption SDK requests a data key from AWS KMS and encrypts each file on the on-premises server, so only ciphertext is uploaded and AWS never receives the plaintext object. B is wrong because server-side encryption is applied after Amazon S3 receives the plaintext object, even when the bytes travel over Direct Connect. C is wrong because HTTPS protects data only while it is in transit, and default encryption still encrypts the object after it arrives. D is wrong because DataSync transfers the plaintext file to Amazon S3, which then encrypts it on receipt.

stem: A company stores regulated data in Amazon S3. A regulator requires the company to prove that it can make all of the stored objects unreadable within minutes if the company detects a compromise. The company currently uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Turn on S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for the bucket, and set a one-day retention period.
Add a bucket policy that denies s3:GetObject for every principal, and apply the policy when a compromise occurs.
Turn on automatic key rotation for the SSE-S3 key, and rotate the key when a compromise occurs.
Re-encrypt the objects with a KMS customer managed key, and disable the key when a compromise occurs.

explanation: D is correct. When the objects are encrypted with a customer managed key, disabling that key immediately prevents every decryption request, so the stored ciphertext becomes unreadable across the whole bucket in one action. A is wrong because Object Lock prevents deletion and overwriting but does nothing to stop reads. B is wrong because a deny policy blocks API calls rather than making the data unreadable, and any principal with s3:PutBucketPolicy can remove it. C is wrong because SSE-S3 keys are owned and rotated by Amazon S3, so the customer cannot rotate or disable them.

stem: A security team must produce a monthly report that lists every read of objects in a sensitive Amazon S3 bucket. AWS CloudTrail is enabled for management events only, and the trail delivers log files to a separate S3 bucket. The team wants to query the records with SQL. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Turn on S3 server access logging for the sensitive bucket, and deliver the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Configure the trail to log CloudTrail data events for the sensitive S3 bucket.
Configure the trail to log CloudTrail Insights events for the AWS account.
Query the delivered log files with Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights.
Create a table for the delivered log files, and query the files with Amazon Athena.

explanation: B is correct. Object-level operations such as GetObject are recorded only when the trail logs CloudTrail data events for the bucket, because management events do not include object-level API calls. E is correct. The delivered CloudTrail log files in Amazon S3 can be cataloged as a table and queried with SQL in Amazon Athena. A is wrong because S3 server access logs are delivered to an S3 bucket rather than to CloudWatch Logs, and their format is not the CloudTrail record the team needs. C is wrong because Insights events report unusual API call rates, not individual object reads. D is wrong because CloudWatch Logs Insights queries log groups, and this trail delivers to Amazon S3.

stem: A company must let auditors run SQL queries against three years of AWS CloudTrail events from every account in its AWS Organizations organization. The company does not want to build or maintain tables, partitions, or crawlers for the audit data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an organization trail that delivers events to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler, and query the data with Amazon Athena.
Create an organization event data store in AWS CloudTrail Lake, and have the auditors run CloudTrail Lake queries.
Send CloudTrail events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs in each account. Run cross-account queries with CloudWatch Logs Insights.
Stream CloudTrail events to an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Give the auditors access to OpenSearch Dashboards.

explanation: B is correct. An organization event data store in CloudTrail Lake collects events from every account, retains them for years, and runs SQL queries directly, with no tables, partitions, or crawlers to manage. A is wrong because the crawler, the partitions, and the table definitions are exactly the maintenance the company wants to avoid. C is wrong because it requires configuring CloudTrail delivery and cross-account observability in every account, and retaining three years of events in CloudWatch Logs costs far more than an event data store. D is wrong because an OpenSearch domain must be sized, patched, and loaded through a delivery pipeline, which is more operational work than a managed event data store.

stem: An AWS Glue job writes application logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. After a failed run, a data engineer must find every log entry that contains a specific error string within a five-minute window and must count the entries by error type. The engineer needs results immediately and cannot provision new infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Export the log group to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler for the exported files, and query the files with Amazon Athena.
Create a metric filter on the log group for the error string. Review the resulting metric in an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard.
Run a CloudWatch Logs Insights query on the log group that filters the error string and aggregates counts by error type.
Subscribe an Amazon Kinesis Data Streams stream to the log group. Process the records with an AWS Lambda function.

explanation: C is correct. CloudWatch Logs Insights queries the existing log group over a chosen time range, filters on the error string, and aggregates counts with a stats command, all without creating any resources. A is wrong because exporting and crawling the logs takes time and creates resources the engineer must then manage. B is wrong because a metric filter evaluates only log events that arrive after the filter is created, so it cannot analyze the run that already failed. D is wrong because a stream and a Lambda function are new infrastructure, and the subscription would not deliver the log events that already exist.

stem: A company collects 2 TB of application logs each day in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Support engineers must search the logs with full-text queries and must view interactive dashboards that refresh within seconds. The company wants a managed solution that does not require the engineers to write SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Export the logs to Amazon S3 each day. Create external tables in Amazon Redshift Spectrum, and build dashboards on the tables.
Send the logs to an Amazon EMR cluster. Use Apache Hive to index the logs, and build dashboards from the Hive tables.
Store the logs in Amazon S3. Query the logs with Amazon Athena, and build the dashboards on the Athena results.
Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter that streams the logs to an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Use OpenSearch Dashboards.

explanation: D is correct. A subscription filter streams log events to Amazon OpenSearch Service in near real time, and OpenSearch provides a full-text search engine with OpenSearch Dashboards for interactive visualizations that need no SQL. A is wrong because Redshift Spectrum requires SQL and a daily export adds hours of latency to the dashboards. B is wrong because an EMR cluster must be operated by the company and Hive uses a SQL-like query language rather than full-text search. C is wrong because Athena is a SQL engine, and per-query scan latency does not support dashboards that refresh within seconds.

stem: A company has an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster in a producer account. A team in a consumer account must query several schemas from that cluster without copying the data. Both clusters use RA3 nodes and are in the same AWS Region. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Unload the schemas to Amazon S3, and create external tables in the consumer cluster with Redshift Spectrum.
Take a snapshot of the producer cluster, and restore the snapshot in the consumer account every night.
In the producer cluster, create a datashare with the schemas, and grant usage to the consumer account.
In the consumer cluster, create a database from the datashare after the producer account authorizes the share.
In the consumer account, create an AWS Glue crawler that connects to the producer cluster and catalogs all of the schemas.

explanation: C is correct. The producer cluster owns the datashare, so the producer adds the schemas to the datashare and grants usage to the consumer account. D is correct. After the producer account authorizes the datashare, the consumer creates a database from it and queries live data with no copy. A is wrong because unloading to Amazon S3 creates a copy of the data, which the requirement prohibits. B is wrong because restoring a snapshot every night creates a full duplicate cluster and the data is stale between restores. E is wrong because a crawler only records metadata and grants the consumer cluster no ability to read the producer's tables.

stem: A company must ensure that data in its AWS Organizations organization never leaves the eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 Regions. Developers in member accounts have permissions to create Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon Redshift snapshots, and AWS Glue jobs. The company must block resource creation and data copies in all other Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM permissions boundary in each member account that allows only the two approved Regions.
Create an AWS Config rule that flags resources in other Regions, and delete the flagged resources with an AWS Lambda function.
Turn off all other Regions in the AWS Billing console for every member account in the organization.
Attach an SCP that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not one of the two approved Regions.

explanation: D is correct. An SCP attached at the organization root denies any action whose aws:RequestedRegion falls outside the approved list, so no principal in any member account, including account administrators, can create resources or copy data into another Region. A is wrong because a permissions boundary must be attached to every principal in every account and can be changed by an account administrator. B is wrong because it detects and removes resources only after the data has already been written outside the approved Regions. C is wrong because only opt-in Regions can be disabled; Regions that are enabled by default cannot be turned off this way.

stem: An auditor asks a company to show every configuration change that was made to its Amazon Redshift clusters and Amazon S3 buckets during the past year, including the settings before and after each change. The company must provide a change timeline for each individual resource. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Turn on AWS Config to record the two resource types, and use the configuration timeline for each resource.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail Insights, and review the anomalies that CloudTrail detects for each of the resources.
Turn on Amazon S3 server access logging and Amazon Redshift audit logging. Query with Amazon Athena.
Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor, and review the security checks for the two resource types every month.

explanation: A is correct. AWS Config records a configuration item every time a recorded resource changes and presents a per-resource configuration timeline that shows the previous and current settings for each change. B is wrong because CloudTrail Insights surfaces unusual API call volumes and does not produce a per-resource history of configuration states. C is wrong because access logs and audit logs record data access and query activity, not configuration changes to the resources. D is wrong because Trusted Advisor evaluates the current state against best practice checks and retains no history of configuration changes.

stem: A company uses Amazon Macie to find sensitive data in an Amazon S3 data lake. Macie detects passport numbers and email addresses, but it does not detect the company's internal employee ID, which always has the format EMP followed by eight digits. The company must include employee IDs in Macie findings. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Add the employee ID format to a Macie allow list, and run the sensitive data discovery job again on the bucket.
Enable Macie automated sensitive data discovery, and increase the sampling depth of the discovery job.
Create a Macie custom data identifier with a regular expression for the format, and add it to the job.
Create an AWS Glue PII detection transform for the format, and run the transform before the Macie job.

explanation: C is correct. A custom data identifier defines a regular expression, and optional keywords and proximity rules, so Macie detects a company-specific format such as EMP followed by eight digits and reports it in the findings of any job that includes the identifier. A is wrong because an allow list tells Macie to ignore matching text, which suppresses findings instead of producing them. B is wrong because automated discovery and deeper sampling still use only the identifiers that Macie already knows, which exclude the internal format. D is wrong because a Glue transform detects and redacts values inside a Glue job and contributes nothing to Macie findings.

stem: A company wants business teams to find and request access to curated datasets without contacting the data engineering team for each request. Data owners must approve or reject each request, and every approval must be recorded. The company already uses Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.text: Store dataset descriptions on a wiki page. Ask the business teams to open a ticket for each dataset that they need.
Publish the datasets as assets in Amazon SageMaker Catalog. Let data owners approve the subscription requests.
Grant every business team read access to the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Let teams query any table that they discover.
Create an AWS Lambda function that adds each requester's IAM role to the data lake bucket policy automatically.

explanation: B is correct. SageMaker Catalog publishes datasets as assets that business teams can search and subscribe to, and the owner of each asset approves or rejects the subscription request while the catalog records the decision and provisions the access. A is wrong because a wiki and a ticket queue keep the data engineering team in the path of every request. C is wrong because open catalog access removes the owner approval step entirely and leaves no record of who was granted what. D is wrong because automatic bucket policy updates grant access with no approval, and the bucket policy grows with every requester.

stem: A company wants to sell curated datasets to external customers who have their own AWS accounts. The company must control which customers receive each dataset, must deliver updates automatically, and must avoid building a subscription and entitlement system. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Publish the datasets as products on AWS Data Exchange, and manage entitlements through the service.
Create a presigned Amazon S3 URL for each dataset file, and email the URLs to the customers every month.
Create an IAM user for each customer in the company's account, and give each user access keys for the bucket.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy the datasets into a bucket that each customer owns.

explanation: A is correct. AWS Data Exchange publishes datasets as products, controls which subscribers are entitled to each product, and delivers new revisions to entitled subscribers automatically, so the company builds no subscription system of its own. B is wrong because presigned URLs expire, must be regenerated for every file and every customer, and carry no entitlement management. C is wrong because IAM users hand long-lived credentials to external parties and still require manual access management for each dataset. D is wrong because replication must be configured for every destination bucket, requires permissions in each customer account, and provides no entitlement or revision control.
